newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude up with NYMEX, talk of ANS deal.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude up with NYMEX, talk of ANS deal.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices rose Thursday in line with higher futures prices amid rumors Alaskan crude sold at a sharply lower discount, dealers said.
Refiners said a typical Alaskan seller, based in Houston, Texas, sold a cargo of benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) grade at $2.10 below July West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
The buyer, rumored to be a Northwest refiner, was not available for comment.
The previous deal, done May 23, was priced at $1.75 under.

High volumes of imports, especially Ecuadorian and other South American grades, have undercut ANS prices in recent month, causing the discount to widen from 91 cents under in March to $1.75 in late May.
Meanwhile, traders said Chevron's refinery south of Los Angeles had shut a crude disillation unit over the weekend.
Heavier California grades remained unchanged this week.
